Provider pools

One local model served by several self-hosted machines: sticky conversations, failover and draining inside GateFox, without a separate router.

About 4 min read · 4 sections

On this page
01 Configuration 02 Where a request goes 03 Observing 04 Limits

A pool serves one model name from several interchangeable machines. Each machine is an ordinary provider with its own picker row; the pool is a provider whose pool field lists them.

qwen/qwen3.8-flash-next (pool) ─┬─ qwen-1 → machine one
                                └─ qwen-2 → machine two

Configuration

[
  { "id": "qwen", "type": "chat-completions-api", "pool": ["qwen-1", "qwen-2"],
    "baseUrl": "http://former-router.example/v1", "tailnet": true, "selfHosted": true,
    "credentialFile": "/private/qwen.key", "models": { "qwen/flash": "flash" } },
  { "id": "qwen-1", "type": "chat-completions-api", "baseUrl": "http://100.64.0.1:4001/v1",
    "tailnet": true, "selfHosted": true, "capacityDiscovery": true,
    "credentialFile": "/private/qwen.key", "models": { "qwen-1/flash": "flash" } },
  { "id": "qwen-2", "type": "chat-completions-api", "baseUrl": "http://100.64.0.2:4001/v1",
    "tailnet": true, "selfHosted": true, "capacityDiscovery": true,
    "credentialFile": "/private/qwen.key", "models": { "qwen-2/flash": "flash" } }
]

The pool and its 2 to 8 members must be chat-completions-api providers on loopback or the tailnet with selfHosted: true, so a pool can never move a conversation to a subscription or a paid API. Every member must serve each pooled model with at least the context window, effort levels and modalities the pool advertises. Members need different base URLs, and each address must reach only its own machine: an address that fronts the whole farm counts every slot twice.

The pool keeps its own baseUrl but never dials it. A release that ignores pool uses that address, so a rollback keeps working while it is served. Adding, removing or changing pool applies live and keeps the model name of saved chats.

Where a request goes

Situation Result
New conversation The member with the most free room on this Mac; a tie is settled by a hash of the conversation.
Known conversation Its own member, which holds its prompt cache. It waits there when the member is full.
New conversation waiting for a full member Moves to another member as soon as one has a free slot.
Member advertises 0 slots (drained) Running work finishes. Waiting requests and conversations move to another member.
Connection refused or dropped, or HTTP 502/503, before any output The request runs on another member. A warm conversation first retries a dropped connection once, after about a second.
Member accepts connections but answers nothing After three unanswered probes in a row, while another member answers, its conversations and silent requests move (45 to 70 seconds).
Request waiting for a member that stops answering Moves without entering it, even while the request ahead keeps its place.
A member just refused or dropped a request It gets no new conversations for 30 seconds, also when it returns sooner.
This Mac loses its network Nobody is lost; conversations return to their own member.
Failure after output began Returned to the client, never replayed. Its retry goes to the same member first.
The model server's own answer (400, 401, 429, 500, empty) Returned unchanged, never moved.
Every member drained Requests wait until one returns or they time out.
Every member unreachable The ordinary retryable upstream_unavailable.

A conversation that moved stays where it moved when the first member returns, so it pays for one cold prefill, not two. Choosing qwen-1/... or qwen-2/... directly always uses that machine, never fails over, and shares its slots with the pool.

A conversation is its thread ID, else its session ID, else its prompt_cache_key. Its member is kept for seven days (at most 4,096 conversations) in the owner-only stateDirectory/provider-pool-ID.json, which holds hashes and member IDs only. A missing or damaged file means the next request chooses again.

Observing

  • gateway availability --json: the pool row lists its members, with their combined health and the sum of their slots. Members have their own rows.
  • gateway diagnostics: providerPools counts requests per member and reason (new, pinned, drained, failover) and each failover.
  • /health advertises provider-pool-v1.

Limits

Each Mac sees its own requests and the slots each machine advertises, not other Macs' load, so two Macs can queue on one machine while another has room. A machine that stops answering in the middle of an answer ends that request through the ordinary silence timeout. Moving a conversation always costs a cold prefill on the new member.
